packet: H5c one standalone receivable-cash refund variant
scope: A receivable_cash_refund links exactly one receivable_cash_allocation targeting standalone receivable. The refund derives its cash_in, treasury_account, target receivable, claim account, party, entity, and currency through typed allocation ancestry.

Each refund is the sole real cash movement: it debits the source treasury once, restores the same claim receivable/net, reverses target settled, consumes dated allocation refund capacity, and adds equal refunded/allocation_reversed measures to the original cash-in allocation root. It does not create cash_out or change gross allocated.

cash_in owns one dated available grant equal to its amount at effective_at. Both cash-in allocation families subtract available while adding gross allocated; refunds post equal refunded/allocation_reversed effects, cancel in available, and leave capacity unchanged. Each receivable_cash_allocation owns one dated refund grant at allocation time.
Refund time must be strictly later than its allocation. Same-time sibling refunds use complete-timestamp refund capacity.
The focused fixture includes both receivable_cash_allocation and sales_invoice_cash_allocation to prove both cash-in allocation families contribute to the source cap.

probe.output: H5c allocated cash refund, dated capacities, source-row oracle, lifecycle rollback, and no-duplicate-cash passed
checks: Cash-in and allocation self-seeds each grant one dated capacity; deletion of all consumers prunes the allocation grant, and deletion/re-addition prunes and recreates the cash-in self-seed cleanly.
A 60 allocation is refunded in partial 20 + same-time sibling 20 + later 20 facts; allocation refund remaining reaches zero and the standalone receivable settlement returns to zero.
Refund at allocation time, currency-inexact amount, zero amount, and cumulative over-refund reject atomically.
Allocation amount/date edits refresh source and refund capacity; cash-in amount/date/party/entity/currency endpoint edits that invalidate descendants reject with full snapshot equality.
Refund amount/date edits, deletion and stable-ID re-addition refresh or prune treasury, claim, settlement, cash-source and allocation-capacity roots together.
Deletion of used allocation, target receivable, and cash-in source is protected; after descendants are removed, the two self-seeded owners can be deleted and recreated.
Independent source-row oracles reconstruct customer receivable/net, target settlement, treasury, gross allocation, refunded/reversed measures, cash-in available capacity, and dated refund capacity.
The disposable graph has no cash_out rows and keeps the unrelated fully allocated sales-invoice cash movement and physical stock root unchanged.

For every cash-in source, the independent complete-time oracle follows each refund through refund.allocation to allocation.source, groups +cash_in.amount, both allocation families' negative amounts, and equal negative-refund/positive-allocation_reversed deltas by timestamp, then checks available.sum and available.instant_min.

limits: This covers standalone receivable allocation refunds only. Invoice refunds, refunds of unallocated cash, physical returns, generic credit notes, and production migration are out of scope.
Gross allocated remains unchanged; refunded and allocation_reversed cancel in the cash-in available equation, so a refund does not create new cash allocation capacity.
No legal, statutory, or production policy interpretation is added.
